findings.evidence: packages/core/src/backend-configuration.ts:168-178 only rejects an expired environment through derived view.status; line 152 deliberately calls environmentFor with both hold exemptions. packages/core/src/projects.ts:138-146 returns active delivery/ready allocation status before checking environment.expiresAt. The metadata reader at backend-configuration.ts:29-35 uses the same derived status. An ordinary timed preview with an existing ready database allocation, no deliveryPreviews record and a deadline that has just elapsed remains available and is shown as prepared.
findings.refutation: Delivery-managed previews do have a separate expiry-derived deliveryHold. That covers deliveryPreviews rows, not the independent preview environments created by the project/environment feature. configureBackend already checks raw environment.expiresAt at lines 88-90, but applicationLifecycleGuard and backendConfiguration do not call that mutation path. The bug therefore survives the existing guard and does not require forged inputs or deployment qualification.
findings.suggestion: Independently reject elapsed environment.expiresAt in the runtime guard and mark the metadata view held, regardless of allocation/delivery status; add a clock-crossing preview test with a ready allocation and current configuration revisions.
